data.why: A street in section: the curb inlet on the left, the pipe sloping right under the road to a river channel at the right end of the cut, which is there from the first frame. The camera opens close on the curb, follows the water and the tennis ball down the pipe to the river, and ends on the whole street.

ideas.idea: the hole is dug by the curb
the street floods into a pond
a pipe grows from the hole down to the river
leaves and the ball wash down and jam the pipe
a grate covers the hole and catches leaves
sand slips through the grate and piles in the pipe
a chamber under the grate fills and the sand sinks to its floor
the catch basin glows
water shoots back up out of the grate and floods the street
a big main grows under the street and the flood drains
the river turns brown as the ball shoots out
a tank fills and holds the surge
the outflow cuts into the bank and it collapses
rocks pile up around the outlet
the river rises over the outlet and water runs back up to the grate
the flap swings open then shut
the street floods again
the pump spins and lifts water over into the river
the pump stops
the generator appears and the pump runs again
grit piles up in the tank
shafts rise to the street with iron covers
the manhole covers glow
the street drains through the grate and the ball floats out to the river
the finished drain rests under the street, the flap open

chain.shows: the hole fills and the street floods
leaves and the tennis ball jam the open pipe
fine sand slips through the grate into the pipe
water shoots back out of the grate
the main dumps the storm into the river, which turns brown
the outflow cuts the riverbank and it collapses
the river rises and runs back up the pipe
the shut flap traps the rain and the street floods
the power fails and the pump stops
grit piles up in the tank and basin

surprises.claim: A catch basin has a sump below its outlet pipe where sand and grit settle out.

surprises.claim: A detention tank holds storm water and releases it slowly to the river.
surprises.search: stormwater detention tank holds runoff releases slowly

surprises.claim: A flap gate opens when water flows out and is forced shut when the river is higher.
surprises.search: flap gate storm drain outfall opens outflow closes river high

surprises.claim: Storm water pump stations lift water over a closed flap gate when the river is high.

sentences.text: If you dig a hole beside the curb, you have a drain.
But the hole fills, and the street becomes a pond.
So you run a pipe to the river.
But leaves, sand and a tennis ball clog the pipe.
So you cover the hole with a grate.
But fine sand slips through the grate into the pipe.
So a chamber below lets the sand sink.
This is a catch basin.
But every basin on the street feeds one small pipe.
So you connect them to a much larger main.
But the main dumps the whole storm into the river.
So you add a tank that holds the surge.
But the tank's outflow washes away the riverbank.
So you pile heavy rocks around the outlet.
But the river rises over the rocks and flows back.
So a flap lets water push it open; the river forces it shut.
But with the flap shut, the rain has nowhere to go.
So you add a pump that lifts the water over.
But a storm cuts the power, and the pump stops.
So a backup generator keeps the pump running.
But trapped grit piles up while the pump runs.
So you add shafts with heavy iron covers.
Those are the manholes you drive over.
Now rain runs past the curb, through the grate, to the river.
Congratulations, you have built a storm drain.
